conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello Mr. Johnson, I'm Dr. Patel. I understand you've been having fevers. Can you tell me more about what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I’ve had a fever for a few days now, along with nausea and vomiting. No belly pain though. I was worried because of my history with the bile ducts.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. Given your past cholangiocarcinoma and stents, we need to be careful. We’ll run some tests to check for infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I remember last time it was a stent issue. Should we be worried about that again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s possible. We’ve ordered blood work and a chest X-ray to start. Your vitals look stable—no fast heart rate or low oxygen.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. And my blood pressure is okay? I’ve been on atenolol for migraines.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your BP is 120 over 72—perfect. We’ll keep you on atenolol unless something changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your chest X-ray was clear, no pneumonia. We also did an ultrasound of your liver.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And what did it show?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The liver looks a bit coarse, and your left lobe is still atrophic. Your spleen is enlarged, but that’s been stable. No fluid or masses.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. But could this be related to the fever?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly. Your labs showed a high band count—13%—which suggests infection. We’re starting IV meropenem because of your history with resistant E. coli.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Meropenem again? That’s strong stuff.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, but given your past infections, we want to cover all bases. Blood cultures are negative so far, which is reassuring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright. What’s next?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve scheduled an MRCP today to get a better look at your bile ducts and stents.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The MRCP is back. It shows multifocal cholangitis—so inflammation in several bile duct areas—especially on the right side.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that why I’m sick?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, likely. There’s also concern that your left stent might be partially blocked, which could be causing the inflammation upstream.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can we fix that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve scheduled an ERCP tomorrow to clean out the stent. The goal is to clear any debris and restore flow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had those before. They’re not fun, but I’ll do it if it helps.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll monitor you closely. Also, your platelets are low—85—so we’ll watch for bleeding risk.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s been low for a while. Is it worse now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Stable. Likely due to your chronic liver issues and past treatments. We’ll keep an eye on it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi Mr. Johnson. The ERCP was partially successful. We cleared some debris from the left stent, but there was bleeding from the bile duct.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Bleeding? Is that serious?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s called hemobilia. It’s rare but can happen after stent manipulation. The good news is it stopped on its own.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No surgery needed?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No. Your hemoglobin stayed stable, and you’re not tachycardic. We didn’t need a CT angiogram or embolization.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank goodness. So the stent is clear now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Partially. We cleared the left side, but the right stent wasn’t accessed due to the bleeding. We’ll monitor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the infection?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve been afebrile since yesterday. Liver enzymes are improving. We’ll continue meropenem for 7 days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I feel better already.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs today show your white count is trending down, and transaminases are improving. Still no growth in blood cultures.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it was likely the bile duct infection?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. The cholangitis explains the fever and nausea. The antibiotics are working.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my diabetes? I’m usually diet-controlled.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve you on sliding scale insulin while you’re here. Your glucose was 200 on admission—stress can raise it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Makes sense. I’ll go back to diet after discharge?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, unless your levels stay high. We’ll check again before you leave.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. No fever, eating normally, and labs keep improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can I go home soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly by Friday. We want to finish your antibiotic course and make sure you’re stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the bleeding? Should I watch for that at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The risk is low now. If you notice black stools or feel lightheaded, call us. But it’s unlikely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Today’s the sixth day of antibiotics. You’ve had no fever, and your labs are stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So one more day?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. We’ll discharge you tomorrow. We’ll review your meds and follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I need to see my oncologist?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. The MRCP showed no new tumor, but the area near the stents is still suspicious. Your oncologist will decide next steps.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And my stents—will I need another ERCP?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly. If symptoms return, we may need to address the right stent. But for now, you’re stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Final day. You’ve completed your antibiotics, labs are good, and you’re feeling well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. What do I need to do at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Resume your usual meds—atenolol, tamsulosin, pantoprazole. Watch for fever, abdominal pain, or jaundice.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And if I get a fever again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Call your doctor or go to the ER. It could mean another infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. Thank you for taking care of me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’ll see you in follow-up. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You’re cleared to go home. Your discharge summary is ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. I’m ready to get back to my routine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just remember: follow up with your gastroenterologist and oncologist. And call if anything changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care, Mr. Johnson. We’re glad you’re feeling better.
